summary: Round 4, test-reviewer lane (testability the rows prescribe; no code, no tests staged -- three documentation files). All four round-3 minors are addressed as raised, and every new factual claim re-verified against the tree holds: GoldenCheckpointTest.java:24-35 does record BOTH measured results the golden-order clause now cites (delete-the-sort green across all three, Map.copyOf failing theGoldenBytesCarryStreamsAndPodsInASCENDINGOrder 6 of 6); CheckpointWriterContentTest.java:143 really is everyDeltas=1 and CheckpointWriter.java:157 really does checkpoint on every delta at that setting, so 'unsatisfiable without changing it' is exact; Checkpoint.pods really is Map<String,Long> (Checkpoint.java:42-44) and decode really does compare one constant (:151); CheckpointCursor.newest really does let IOException out (:67-73); ChainEntry.java:50 really does record ADR-0032 consuming the reserved kind; ADR-0028:130 really does leave the version path open; the M3.0 quotation matches backlog-done.md:93. baselines/review.txt's 'eleven findings ... six of them major' now matches the two round-1 artifacts. Nothing was deleted that was load-bearing: the two withdrawn prescriptions (KIND-vs-VERSION, the bare bump) were wrong and their replacement defers to the ADR while adding a real constraint (old objects must still decode). BUT THE ANSWER TO THE QUESTION ASKED IS NO: I found another mutation that survives the whole set, and it survives BECAUSE of the assertion added this round. The new clause pins the RETURNED offsets and the sequencer's nextOffset. Neither can see what is APPENDED TO THE CHAIN, because ChainReplay.java:441 folds with Math::max -- so a replay whose original runs are spliced into the delta that gets PUT is green on every prescription and leaves the chain carrying one run twice, which Invariants.java:127-134 calls an I2 violation. And that is not a deviation an implementer has to choose: CommitLog.java:328-334 encodes, PUTs and RETURNS one object, so appending is what building the returned delta DOES. One major, three minors.
verified_from_round_3: T4 (the returned OFFSETS were unpinned) -- ADDRESSED for the mutation as raised. backlog-notes.md:305-311 names current-state offsets verbatim and requires the ORIGINAL ones; :313-318 deletes the false 'survives either way' claim from the parent section (:185-187 now reads 'DEPENDS on M4.10c's outcome') and states why Map<String,Long> can detect but not answer. Against the mutation I named, a replay's returned firstOffset would be the stream's current nextOffset rather than the original base, so an equality assertion on the first delta's per-run firstOffset fails. Sufficient for THAT mutation. Not sufficient for the one in finding T8, which the fix's own choice of assertion target creates.

T5 (a commit after the last checkpoint was satisfiable by a fixture whose asserted pod was checkpointed anyway; and unsatisfiable at everyDeltas=1) -- ADDRESSED for the mutation as raised, and it opens the symmetric one. :261-264 now requires 'a value that only that commit could supply' and says the everyDeltas setting must change. Verified satisfiable: everyDeltas=2 with an odd number of predecessor commits leaves a delta uncovered by the last checkpoint, and asserting the pod committed only in it kills checkpoint-only recovery. See finding T9 for what the same sentence now permits.

T6/P11 (the round-2 fix disarmed the golden order detector) -- ADDRESSED AND CORRECT. :268-276 requires order in BOTH tiers, names delete-the-sort as the codec test's mutation and Map.copyOf as the golden's, and attributes the 6-of-6 figure to GoldenCheckpointTest's javadoc, where it is (:31-35, 'fails theGoldenBytesCarryStreamsAndPodsInASCENDINGOrder in 6 of 6 fresh runs'). I re-walked both mutations: CheckpointTest.theENCODERSortsWhateverOrderTheCallerHandedIn reads the ENCODED order so it dies on a deleted sort and cannot see the record's copy; the golden test decodes committed bytes so it dies on Map.copyOf and cannot see a deleted sort. Two mutations, two tiers, correctly assigned. 'Dropping either tier disarms one mutation' is exactly right.

T7 (baselines/review.txt said six findings where there were eleven) -- ADDRESSED. baselines/review.txt:28 now reads 'eleven findings at round 1 across the two roles, six of them major', which matches .harness/review/acf50ad67afe* (3 major + 2 minor reviewer, 3 major + 3 minor test-reviewer).

findings.title: The new offsets prescription pins the RETURNED delta and the sequencer's nextOffset -- neither of which can see the replayed runs being APPENDED TO THE CHAIN, because the chain fold is Math::max and the returned object IS the appended object
findings.failure_scenario: SURVIVING MUTATION: on a replayed (podId, flushSeq), do not create a new offset assignment -- reuse the ORIGINAL RunCommits -- but leave them in the CommitDelta that CommitLog builds, encodes, PUTs and returns. Concretely, in CommitLog.commitSubmissions (CommitLog.java:310-334) the replayed submission's runs are constructed from the remembered base instead of `cursor.computeIfAbsent(key, this::nextOffset)`, and everything downstream is untouched. Walk every prescription M4.10d now carries. (a) ':305-311, the replay must return the ORIGINAL offsets' -- GREEN, the returned delta literally carries the original firstOffsets, which is the whole point of the mutation. (b) ':320-328, a replayed pair must leave nextOffset UNCHANGED' -- GREEN, and this is the load-bearing part: ChainReplay.java:433-443 folds a delta with `into.merge(run.key(), run.lastOffset() + 1, Math::max)`, so re-appending run r at firstOffset 100 count 4 when the stream already stands at 104 leaves nextOffset at 104. The assertion the row calls 'THE ASSERTION THAT KILLS IT' is structurally blind to a re-append. (c) ':287-295, the retrying caller gets its submitted segment key back' -- GREEN, the key is in the returned delta. (d) ':279-285, a restarted pod reissuing 0 for a NEW segment is ACCEPTED' -- GREEN, unaffected. (e) '< for <=' -- GREEN. (f) 'per-pod map, not a fleet-wide long' -- GREEN. (g) 'survives a takeover' -- GREEN. WHAT SHIPS: the commit chain now carries run r twice, in two deltas at two sequences, with the same absolute offsets. sequencer/src/test/java/binjava/sequencer/Invariants.java:127-134 classifies exactly this as an I2 violation ('stream ... resumes at 100, before 104'), and I2 -- offsets never reassigned -- is the invariant the parent M4.10 row's 'silent duplication that _id dedup would mask inconsistently' names. WHY THIS IS THE DEFAULT AND NOT AN EXOTIC CHOICE: CommitLog.java:328-334 builds ONE CommitDelta, PUTs its encoding, applies it and returns THAT SAME OBJECT. There is no seam today between 'what is appended' and 'what is returned', so an implementer who satisfies :305-311 by putting the original runs into the returned delta appends them for free, with no line of code expressing an intent to. The row never says the two must differ. AND THE BATCHED PATH FORCES IT: Sequencer.java:111 makes commitAll the primitive (commit delegates via List.of), a batch mixes several pods' flushes, and if one member is a replay the implementation MUST append the new members while not appending the replayed one -- the only shape that satisfies both :287-295 (the replayed segment must be in the return) and 'append nothing' (:306). No row mentions the batched case at all; every prescription is written for a single replayed request, and a test suite of single-request replays cannot distinguish 'appended nothing' from 'appended the original runs again'. THE MISSING PRESCRIPTIONS, both cheap because the tree already has the instruments: (1) assert on the CHAIN, not only on nextOffset and the reply -- after the replay, either no new delta exists at all or the delta at the new sequence carries no run for the replayed segment key; and run the resulting chain through Invariants.checkChain requiring zero I2 violations, which is precisely the detector this project built for this class of bug. (2) name the batched case: a commitAll carrying one replayed request and one new request must append the new one, must not append the replayed one, and must return BOTH -- a batch-level refusal (drop the whole batch when any member replays) silently loses the co-batched flush while passing every criterion above, and Sequencer.java:107-109 promises 'the durable delta carrying every submitted segment'.

findings.title: The T5 fix closes checkpoint-only recovery and opens the symmetric hole: a recovery that reads the deltas after the checkpoint and IGNORES checkpoint.pods() now passes the prescribed anchor, and that is the parent row's headline case
findings.failure_scenario: SURVIVING MUTATION: seed the recovered idempotency window from the deltas AFTER the newest checkpoint only -- initialise it empty and never read `checkpoint.pods()`. Build the fixture exactly as :261-264 now requires: everyDeltas raised off 1, predecessor commits podz twice (the second triggering a checkpoint carrying {podz: 2}), then commits poda 42 with no checkpoint after it, then takeover, then assert the successor's first checkpoint carries poda -> 42, a value only the post-checkpoint delta could supply. GREEN under the mutation, because poda -> 42 is reconstructed from the uncovered delta and nothing in the fixture asks about podz. WHAT SHIPS: every pod whose last commit is BEHIND the newest checkpoint has no window entry after a takeover, so its retry is accepted and its offsets are assigned twice -- 'the case where the replay arrives after a checkpoint recorded it', which is the parent M4.10 row's own headline and M4.10d's opening line at :277-278. Note the shape: at round 3 the fixture pinned the checkpoint path and nothing else; the fix inverted it to pin the delta path and nothing else, which is review.md rule two-round-cap's recorded lesson ('every extra round found defects in the previous round's fix') happening inside this row. THE ACCURATE FORM IS BOTH, and it costs one extra pod in the same fixture: assert one pod whose value ONLY the last checkpoint holds AND one pod whose value ONLY the post-checkpoint delta holds. Either alone is half a detector. Minor rather than major only because M4.10d:313-318 names the post-checkpoint scenario to the session that writes the dedup tests, so the hole is likely found one row later rather than shipped -- but it is found after M4.10c has landed green.

findings.title: The requirement that the durable window carry the ANSWER, not only the detection, is stated only in the two sections the LAST session reads -- not in the row that decides the format list, nor in the row that changes the formats
findings.failure_scenario: ORDERING FAILURE, not a mutation. :313-318 establishes that answering a post-checkpoint replay needs original offsets in the recovered window, and :185-187 repeats it in the split banner. Neither #m410b nor #m410c says so. Per .agents/skills/next-task/SKILL.md a session reads the notes for the task it picks: the M4.10b session reads :194-216, whose stated output is 'A LIST OF FORMATS' for making the KEY durable, with no mention of the answer; the M4.10c session reads :217-276, which describes Checkpoint's pods as Map<String, Long>, prescribes folding the recovered window into CheckpointWriter.pods, and anchors on `poda -> 42` -- a bare long, i.e. exactly the shape :314-315 says 'is enough to DETECT a replay and nothing to ANSWER one'. So b's ADR decides the format list without the requirement, c changes both formats to that list, and d then cannot satisfy its own :311 without either (i) a SECOND format change, which is the second ADR, second golden set and second atomic commit that :177-181 gives as the whole reason this task was split at the point of picking it up, or (ii) quietly scoping its offsets assertion to replays still inside the delta window, which is the parent row's headline case going untested with every prescription green. THE MISSING SENTENCE is one clause in #m410b -- the ADR must say what the durable window carries to ANSWER a retry, not only to detect one -- and its echo in #m410c's list of what changes. Minor because the requirement does exist in the tree and in the banner; the defect is that it is unreadable from where the deciding work happens.

findings.title: 'QUALIFY THE VALUE, NOT THE KEY' is a prescription of exactly the class this round deleted twice, sitting ten lines above the sentence renouncing it, and it leaves the row's own anchor assertion describing the un-widened value
findings.failure_scenario: TWO CONCRETE CONSEQUENCES. (1) :238-239 says 'this row does NOT prescribe how -- an earlier draft did, wrongly, twice', and the commit body records that the KIND-vs-VERSION mechanism and the bare bump were removed because neither is a decomposition row's decision. :228-232 then decides the pods entry's SHAPE -- which is verbatim M4.10b's job at :194 ('DECIDE THE IDEMPOTENCY KEY AND WHERE IT IS CARRIED'). That reproduces round-1 finding P1: the ADR either ratifies an answer already written into c, or contradicts it and c's row is stale from the day it is read. The size argument the clause rests on is also cited one section off -- ADR-0033's Context rejects growth with the number of COMMITS (the offset-to-segment index); what rejects growth per (epoch, pod) is its Consequences, 'The size stays bounded by the fleet, not by uptime'. The constraint is real and citable; the prescription drawn from it is stronger than the constraint, since pruning a qualified key to the newest epoch per pod also stays O(pods) and is forbidden by the literal wording. (2) The prescription and the anchor disagree inside one section: :255-257 requires asserting `poda -> 42`, which is the value under TODAY's Map<String, Long>. If the value is widened as :232 demands, the entry is no longer 42L and the assertion as written cannot be the one that lands. It fails loudly rather than passing vacuously, so nothing ships past it -- but the row now names a literal expected value it has itself made wrong. THE ACCURATE FORM: state the CONSTRAINT the ADR must satisfy ('whatever carries the qualification, the pods section stays O(pods) -- ADR-0033's Consequences') and leave the shape, and the anchor's expected value, to it.

not_findings_but_worth_the_commit_body: The everyDeltas claim is exact and I checked the mechanism rather than the sentence: CheckpointWriter.java:157 triggers on `deltasSinceCheckpoint >= everyDeltas`, and the takeover fixture at CheckpointWriterContentTest.java:143 passes 1, so at that setting no commit can be after the last checkpoint. 'The fixture must change that setting' is the right instruction and is satisfiable.

The golden-order clause is the only place in this diff where a prescription is strictly stronger than what I asked for at round 3 and is also correct: it names two different mutations, assigns each to the tier measured to catch it, and cites the measurement rather than asserting it. That is the shape the other clauses should copy.

No test file is staged, no assertion anywhere in the tree was loosened, and nothing in this diff deletes a prescription that was doing work -- the two deletions removed statements that were false about the formats, and both are replaced by a deferral plus a new constraint (old objects must still decode) that is stronger than what it replaced.

M4.10d:330-334 still discloses plainly that no production caller replays a pair today and that the row must either add the retry path or say its coverage stops at the sequencer seam. That disclosure is what keeps finding T8's chain assertion honest about which tier it can live in -- CommitLog and Invariants.checkChain are both reachable at T0/T1 with MemoryBinStore, so no socket, clock or object store is needed for any of it.
